chapter: Steamer Capitol and New Orleans bands
title: Cousin Dejean; leaving on the Capitol with Desvigne in 1936
summary: Fused exchanges about Harold Dejean, then Justin leaves New Orleans on the steamer Capitol with Sidney Desvigne, falls ill in St. Paul and settles in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I haven't seen him in about three or four years since, of course I've been away from New Orleans for quite some time now since. When did you leave about? Well I left in 1936. And he played a parade a couple of weeks ago.
Al Crocise has his own band now. Well, he has his own band now.
Oh is that right? I haven't seen him. I haven't seen him in about three or four years since, of course I've been away from New Orleans for quite some time now since. When did you leave about?

I left there on the Steema Capitol. I was playing with Sidney Desveen at the time. And we played the boat for that summer. Went all the way up the river. All the way to St. Paul, yes. So I left the unit in St. Paul because I got pretty sick. And I started going back to New Orleans where I just came here to Chicago since my closest relatives was here. And I've been here ever since. Of course I have been tempted to go back several times during that period but I never did get back.
